snippet.title: Maybe… but I’d like to think I changed social media too
snippet.description: Maybe… but I’d like to think I changed social media too. I created a space where it’s okay to show yourself as you are unfiltered. So as much as social media has left its mark on me, I hope I am leaving a mark on it. I still roll out of bed looking like a hot mess and push the record button. I still share my daily life. I am still open and honest about my struggles not just my successes. Because that’s real life. Over the last 3.5 years I have certainly changed. I have proved to myself I’m capable of so much more than I ever imagined. I have realized it’s okay to ask for help— and take it when it is offered. I have learned that prioritizing myself doesn’t make me a bad mom or wife. I have SO much left to work on, but change isn’t always a bad thing In order to grow into the person I am today change was necessary. The girl who started all of this in 2023 would be so proud of me.

After three years of renovating our abandoned watermill in Portugal, we're finally reaching the point where it can actually function like a home.

But first… we have a problem.

Our gray water system is completely backed up, leaving roughly 250 gallons of water sitting in our pump box. Without getting this working, we can't continuously use the kitchen, finish the bathroom, or eventually live inside the watermill.

So Drew takes on a job neither of us expected to be doing ourselves: figuring out and installing our septic pump system.

Meanwhile, we install our beautiful old market find sink, add a new brass faucet, install our first proper flushing toilet, and finally have running water inside the bathroom!

And then comes some HUGE news: our electrical inspection passed with flying colors, bringing us one major step closer to finally receiving the habitation license we've been working toward for the past three years.

This watermill is finally starting to feel like home.

snippet.description:
Thank you Brooklyn Bedding for sponsoring! Visit http://brooklynbedding.com/weedem to get 30% off your order with my code: WEEDEM

Breeding quality dairy goats is not for the faint of heart. Sometimes you have major defects and sometimes it's simply not desirable. This week we made some hard decisions for the herd.

Hi there! 👋🏻 We live on a 1-acre farm right in the middle of the busy city of Phoenix, Arizona! Our names are Kevin & DaNelle, and we moved here in 2009, when our kids Ethan & Lydia were just 6 & 4 years old 🥰  Over the years we've raised goats for milk, chickens for eggs, built a fish/swim pond, planted fruit & nut trees, and grew a large garden full of veggies. We've also raised a bunch of other animals like pigs, sheep, turkeys, geese, peacocks, and more! 

Now that our kids are away at college, we have settled into doing what we love most -- which is raising & breeding goats ethically to improve genetics. But don't worry, we'll forever love our goofy pet goats like Luna the herd queen & Willow the stump lover. We also still love raising chickens for eggs, gardening, tending to the fruit & nut trees, and growing fish in the pond. We use the fresh goat's milk to make cheese, butter, yogurt -- and we use that + everything else we harvest on our little farm to make delicious meals. Having a getaway from the busy world right in our backyard brings so much joy to us each day, and we hope it brings some to you, too. 🥰
